finding.claim: The DELETE /projects/:id handler calls authorized(), which returns a boolean instead of throwing, and discards the result. The ownership/admin check is never enforced, so any authenticated user can delete any project (broken access control / IDOR). The PUT handler uses authorize(), which throws, so it is enforced correctly. The mix-up of the two similarly named helpers causes the bug.
finding.source: Any authenticated user (req.user) sending DELETE /projects/<victim project id>, where the id is attacker-controlled via req.params.id and the project is owned by someone else.
finding.sink: req.store.projects.delete(project.id) at api.js:19, which permanently deletes the project.

trace.note: Route DELETE /projects/:id; id comes from the URL
Project is loaded by attacker-supplied id with no ownership filter
authorized(req.user, project) returns false for non-owners, but the return value is ignored and nothing throws
authorized() only returns a boolean (resource.ownerId === user.id || user.isAdmin === true) and never throws
Deletion runs unconditionally, then 204 is returned

finding.guards_checked: Checked api.js for a router-level auth middleware or ownership check before the handler. The router has no router.use() middleware and the file defines no other guard. The only guard is the ignored authorized() call. The upstream code that sets req.user and req.store is not in this repo, so authentication itself is assumed. The sibling PUT route at api.js:25 uses the throwing authorize(), which confirms the intended behaviour. Not checked: any app-level guard outside this directory.

verdict.guard_found: Only the authorized() call at api.js:18, which returns a boolean and whose result is discarded. No router.use() middleware exists in this file. The throwing authorize() is used only on the PUT route (api.js:25).
verdict.reason: At api.js:18 the boolean from authorized() (defined at api.js:12-14, never throws) is discarded, so api.js:19 deletes any project for any authenticated user, whereas PUT correctly uses the throwing authorize() at api.js:25.
